text: Well, here's Morris Jessup.
I've been wanting to have a visit with you for a long time.
I hear you're back from Mexico.
Yes, I've been back about six weeks.
I had a very interesting trip down there.
I was able to work with the Mexican government and had access to a million photographs taken
from the air over Mexico.
ago, and from these I have been able to find at least 15 of what I call extraterrestrial
craters, and possibly a number of other ones, although the other ones are too small to verify
from photographs taken at high altitudes. The ones which I have been able to study in
in detail are very large, the biggest one being about a mile and a half across, and
the smallest one about six to eight hundred yards. I'm quite convinced that this group
of craters was made by something arriving on Earth from space, and since the geologists
just tell me that they may not have been made by meteors.
We have to look for other causes as well as meteors.
It's my opinion that these craters were made at the time
when the continent of Atlantis was destroyed
and that the entire Caribbean Sea and Gulf of Mexico area
results from an impact of a very large group of objects from space or from a comet,
and that this physical evidence, which I am uncovering in and near Mexico
and around the Caribbean Gulf of Mexico area,
represents the physical brie and results of the cataclysm
which Immanuel Velikovsky has outlined in his three books.
Well, didn't I hear you say once that you thought there was some similarity
or relationship between those and the type of thing that's visible on the moon, the craters?
As I can make out, these craters in Mexico are identical in appearance with the smaller craters,
which are just barely within the limits of small telescopes
but which are seen with large telescopes.
There are many, many thousands of craters on the moon
that range in size from a half a mile to five or ten miles in diameter,
and these craters are, you might say, laboratory specimens of what exists on the moon.
Not only that, but a large number of them are in geographical areas in Mexico, which
look just like the areas on the moon where these little craters appear, and make an environment
or a surrounding exactly of the same nature as those on the moon, including the desert
or semi-desert conditions so that the craters could be associated with lunar craters one way or another.
Well, where did I hear that hint that these craters might possibly be some kind of hangars for flying saucers?
Did I get that from you or someone else?
It could be. I have considered that.
I haven't found any conclusive evidence for anything like that.
but on the other hand, I have not had much time to spend in the field.
Certainly they are not being used for that purpose at present
because there are people all around them,
and if anything like that was going on, it would be known.
But there are rumors that craters down on the border of Guatemala and Mexico
are being used for that purpose,
and I think Wilkins has reported that in one of his books.
Oh, yeah.
Well, I got your new book today about the UFO and the Bible.
Well, that's just a curtain raiser to the problem of UFO and the Bible.
I've had time to read only the introduction, and I think that is beautifully written.
If the rest of it is like that, it's going to be really worthwhile.
Well, the rest of it is more analytical than the introduction.
it was very difficult to present a problem of such magnitude,
or even to outline a problem of such magnitude, in a short little book like this.
In fact, this book was written as a chapter in the expanding case for the UFO,
which will be out probably in September or October.
But the publishers liked the little story about the Bible so well
that they decided they would just lift it out and make a separate book of it,
so I wrote the introduction after they had done that.
Actually, I have not tried to cover the so-called classic Bible references,
such as Ezekiel's wheel, for instance, or the taking of Elijah to heaven
in a fiery chariot or whatever it may have been.
But I have tried more to perhaps take a philosophical view
and to interpret the spirit of what the Bible has to say to us
rather to set the stage for what which is to come.
I have selected as text, if I may use the preacher's term,
selected the 13th chapter of St. Mark, which seemed to me to cover in a very brief form
almost all possible phases of UFO and space life activity.
And I've used this as a cross-section and just as a sort of a preparation for other work.
In fact, I'm continuing the work right now.
How many more books did you say are in the office?
I would say that three more books on the Bible is the minimum in which I can cover all of the UFO material which I see in the Bible as I'm reading it today.
And the UFO annual, is that coming out again?
Yes?
We're not sure.
Citadel told me to go ahead collecting material.
I just heard from them this past week, this week,
that there certainly will be another volume of this kind.
They're not sure whether they want to make it an annual or a biannual,
but if they make anything, I feel sure it will be an annual
because a biannual doesn't make any sense at all.
It's not current enough.
Well, this is practically your life work now, isn't it?
except I'm the lawnmower at the moment.
Well, the subject owns us.
It's so much bigger than we are.
I don't blame you.
Well, that is certainly the truth.
The subject takes hold of you
and practically become a slave to it.
It's a little hard to explain,
but once you get into it,
you recognize the length and the breadth and the depth of it
to a point where it is not only amazing, but perhaps appalling as well.
I was interested in your view that we were talking about a little while ago,
the philosophical picture.
It wasn't too bright, the way you put it,
but I guess we can all agree that the world is in a state that we've seen before.
The world is certainly in a mess that we can agree on.
Now, whether a new concept will straighten it out or not, I don't know.
I have a friend that I correspond with in Arizona who says it's already too late,
that the human race is beyond saving.
I think that there's a little bit on the pessimistic side,
and if I didn't think it was pessimistic, I don't think I would waste any time writing books.
That wouldn't be worth the effort.
Well, sometimes I'm overwhelmed at what man has done through science.
It's a terrific accomplishment.
There's just something there about his moral nature that doesn't get straightened out.
And I wonder if this new dimension that we're facing, whatever it is,
will perhaps be a means of getting us in balance again.
I think there is a possibility of exactly that.
It certainly is true that all through the 20th century, and perhaps slightly before the beginning of the 20th century,
that science has been running ahead of the man in the street.
And in the past, oh, I'd say the past 30 years, this gap has been widening very seriously,
and in the past 10 years it's been widening at a very alarming rate.
Of course, it's been said that Isaac Newton was the last human being who would ever know all the science of his time, and that was probably true.
But I don't know hardly what can be done about it.
It seems that once, if you try to talk about slowing science up,
immediately everybody screams that you're impeding progress,
and maybe they're right,
but I think sometimes we're computing change with progress
and don't actually know that we aren't truly progressing.
It's certainly true that science has set up a vast framework
of the material or purely mechanical phases of the world we live in, and as far as science has gone,
it has pretty much proved its point and consolidated its gains. But science is just
as bigoted today and just as arrogant as the Church was in the Dark and Middle Ages, and where
where the Church overlooked what most of us consider to be reality,
science is in turn overlooking nearly all of the spiritual values,
and I think both of them have missed the boat.
What we need is a great synthesis.
I think that is exactly right.
I'm writing these books about the Bible, precisely that in mind,
that we should perhaps start another school of thought
which will consolidate what both religion and science have given us from the past.
I think if we don't do something like that and do it very, very quickly,
that the human race is just going to fall apart
for lack of, I might say, intellectual cement.
That's very good.
Well, I'm sure we can't stop science.
The momentum is going too fast.
But it puts a great responsibility on the few
who have vision and who have a synthesizing view of this thing,
try to get it in line.
I think your books are going to play a big part in this,
because I know how sincere you are,
and I also happen to know that you're what I'd call a born researcher.
There aren't too many of those.
Yes, that's true.
And then being a real astronomer, too,
there's not too many of those in this field.
Well, as far as I know, there aren't any other ones in the field
except Mansell, and he's in a completely negative way,
so somebody's got to get in and offset what he has to say on the subject.
Yeah.
We're going to keep on being lopsided in the matter.
Mr. Jeff, I'd like to ask you a few questions.
Okay.
Getting back to your current research on the UFO and the Bible,
in rough figures, just about how many references would you say exist
in the King James Version of the Christian Bible today?
I haven't made an analytical study all the way through the Bible yet.
I have covered in an intense way so far the five books of Moses,
and just in this part of the Bible there certainly are hundreds
hundreds of either direct or indirect references to UFO or related phenomena.
I wouldn't want to be quoted on how many there actually are in the Bible,
because as sure as I am quoted, somebody will go out and count them,
and his interpretation of what's a UFO reference will differ from mine,
and he'll all walk out the Bible, and I do, perhaps,
and so we'll come up with two different things.
but certainly directly and indirectly there must be thousands,
literally thousands, with references in the Bible.
Would you say that's divided equally between the Old Testament and the New Testament,
or do the larger amount of fighting scenes occur in the Old Testament?
I don't think I am yet confident to answer that question quantitatively.
From what I have seen of the Old Testament,
the references are just tremendous.
I think also the Old Testament being a much longer work
that even if you had the same number of references per chapter or book
that the weight of it would be in favor of the Old Testament.
I don't think I can answer that yet until I've completed this study
and I think it will take me a year to complete it.
So quite a long time off.
anticipate any criticism from organized theology in any way at all, any criticism of your books?

I'd like to ask you a few questions about your recent trip to Mexico.
You mentioned something about pictures you had been examining.
Have you been looking at pictures of actual UFO phenomena or mostly...
This was in connection with the crater study.
The Mexican government is very cooperative and very sympathetic to research,
whether it's UFO or any type of research.
And the government unofficially but very kindly made available to me
a whole room full of aerial photographs on which I could search for new examples of the craters
and study their geographical location with respect to each other.
Some of these photographs will undoubtedly, in the long run,
contribute to a solution of what caused the craters
and how long they've been there
and whether or not they're of any use to us or anyone else at present time.
But the work is very preliminary,
and it was only towards the very end of my trip
that I did succeed in getting this very kind cooperation from the government down there.
I went out and climbed into, I believe, a total of eight of the 15 that I know about.
And I personally am thoroughly convinced from the photographs
and from the very quick fieldwork that they were caused by something from space.
Well, most of your trip then was concerned with this crater research instead of UFO?
I did not go to Mexico primarily to study UFO.
I went for two purposes.
One was vacation from writing and all of this heavy pondering and analysis that goes with this type of writing,
and to get out in the open and check into my craters, which I hadn't visited for about four years.
Would you care to make any comment about UFO activity in Mexico in general?
any conversations you might have had down there indirectly as a result of your trip?
I didn't have many conversations directly about UFO.
I found, from talking with three or four different people,
that the officials of the Mexican government are very much concerned about this problem
and much more willing to talk about it than the officials of some other governments that one might name.
And the newspapers are much more open-minded.
I found the staff of La Prensa, for instance, the largest circulation newspaper in Mexico,
to be intensely interested in this problem.
And as soon as they knew of my interest in Mexico and in the craters and in the UFO,
I was dragged around through this big building and introduced to everybody from the elevator boy
on up to the owner and the managing editor.
I might say also that LaPrensa has bought the Mexican rights for the case for the UFO,
and I saw the Spanish translation, also the cover for the book, and it should be off the
press in Spanish within another month, I would say, probably in August.

other direct activities than UFO. Do you care to say anything in conclusion for this tape
in regards to fire sources in general all over the world? Any recent observations on

logical, but that it's real and that it's been here for a long time, I think I will
